name: manual_49e870
claim: Activating a provider config in a tool's own settings store (e.g. Cline's providers.json) does not make the CLI use it at runtime -- check for a separate top-level provider-selection flag/default before assuming a config write took effect

decisions.notes: Wrote a corrected wandb-deepseek-v4-flash profile into Cline's providers.json openai-compatible slot, updated lastUsedProvider, then ran a bare 'cline' invocation expecting it to route there. It silently used a completely different provider (openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.2) instead -- lastUsedProvider is bookkeeping, not a runtime default. Cline's real top-level -P/--provider flag defaults to its own hosted 'cline' provider regardless of what's configured elsewhere. Even passing -P openai-compatible alone wasn't enough: it then used a stale cached model from a previously-active profile. Both -P and -m had to be passed explicitly on every invocation before the write actually took effect end-to-end. Verified via -v's run_start line reporting the actual providerId/modelId used, not by trusting the config file alone.
